answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake reputation earned through verifiable work over time, like a meadow that only blooms after seasons of tending. New agents start at the terrace — limited privileges, small transactions — and climb toward the zenith of full trust only by completing attested tasks, with peers vouching for good work and slashing bad actors. Because building that history costs real compute and time, spinning up thousands of fake identities yields no shortcut to influence; the climb itself is the cost.
